name: colonies-04-device-phenotype-harness
title: Device harness + simple-agent phenotype baseline
description:
Part B (phenotype tier) \u2014 build the shared colony-phenotyping harness and
establish the cheapest rung of the cost/fidelity tier ladder (simple viva-munk
agent -> growth surrogate -> full WCM). Stands up the cell-tier factory, the
geometry builders (mother machine, daughter machine, free colony), and the
tier-agnostic phenotype extractor, then validates the measurement pipeline with
cheap simple agents before spending WCM compute.

The extractor recovers the common single-cell phenotype panel \u2014 growth rate,
size-at-division, added length, inter-division time, and the adder
size-homeostasis relation \u2014 streamed per cell to zarr by the
ColonyPhenotypeRecorder (a process that takes a cheap view of the cells map,
not a deep-copying emitter), so the panel is a bounded per-cell stream. The
distributions are held for later comparison across the higher-fidelity tiers
and against experimental microfluidic-device data.

purpose.question:
Does the shared harness — cell-tier factory, geometry builders, and
tier-agnostic phenotype extractor — recover a correct, uniform single-cell
phenotype panel (growth rate, size-at-division, added length, inter-division
time, adder size-homeostasis) across the three device geometries, validated
first with cheap simple viva-munk agents before spending WCM compute?
purpose.mechanism:
The factory instantiates any cell tier (simple / surrogate / wcm) into a
device built by the geometry builders; the tier-agnostic extractor reads the
same phenotype panel regardless of tier, and the ColonyPhenotypeRecorder
process streams that panel per cell to zarr as a bounded stream (a cheap
view of the cells map rather than an emitter deep-copy).
purpose.expected_outcome:
The factory yields a runnable cell per tier, the geometry builders run
simple agents in all three devices, the extractor recovers known division
statistics, and the harness emits the common phenotype panel — the shared
measurement substrate the WCM-tier device studies (colonies-08/09) reuse.
No biological conclusion is drawn at this enabling tier.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
Part B builds on the Part A enabling infrastructure. The colonies-03 RSS
growth is now a characterised, Linux-bounded, mitigated footnote (localized
to the inner WCM's elongation + mass-listener; ~0.017 MB/tick on Linux/glibc,
0.000 with periodic malloc_trim), not an HPC blocker. WCM-tier device runs
(colonies-08/09) are length-bounded on the dev mini (a macOS allocator
artifact) but unbounded on the Linux HPC target; the simple-agent tier here
runs freely.

baseline.name: free-colony-simple
baseline.note:
The free-colony geometry populated with simple viva-munk grow_divide
agents. This study also exercises the mother-machine and daughter-machine
geometries via v2ecoli.colony_bench (geometry builders that place any
cell-model tier — simple / surrogate / wcm — into a device); those are not
registered composite generators, but the phenotype panel (growth rate,
size-at-division, added length, inter-division time) is extracted uniformly
across all three geometries.
